Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown velvety spots on leaf surfaces, yellowing leaves, premature defoliation, and scabby corky lesions on fruit.
recommendations: Prune branches to improve air circulation and sunlight penetration.
Rake, remove, and destroy fallen leaves and fruit around the tree base.
Apply organic fungicides (like copper or sulfur) early in the growing season.
prevention: Select disease-resistant apple cultivars.
Maintain proper tree spacing.
Avoid overhead watering; irrigate at the soil level.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-rimmed circular leaf spots ('frog-eye' leaf spot), cankers on limbs, and firm brown rot on fruit with concentric bands.
recommendations: Prune out dead limbs, twigs, and cankers during winter dormancy.
Dispose of mummified fruit left hanging on the tree or fallen on the ground.
Apply targeted protective fungicides during the bud-break period.
prevention: Keep trees healthy with proper pruning and fertilization.
Control insects that cause entry wounds on fruit.
Remove dead wood from nearby windbreaks.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright orange or yellow-orange spots on leaf surfaces, followed by small tube-like structures on the leaf undersides.
recommendations: Remove nearby galls on cedar or juniper host trees if present.
Apply appropriate rust-controlling fungicides from pink bud stage through petal fall.
Prune affected twigs containing orange rust pustules.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple cultivars.
Avoid planting apples near red cedars or junipers.
Prune trees to ensure rapid leaf drying after rain.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is green, robust, and free of discoloration or spots. Stems and fruit show normal, healthy growth.
recommendations: Maintain routine watering, mulching, and fertilizing schedules.
Inspect leaves weekly for early signs of pests or disease spores.
Ensure proper branch pruning for sunlight exposure.
prevention: Promote general tree vigor.
Sanitize pruning tools before use.
Practice good weed management.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are dark green, glossy, and show no signs of yellowing, spotting, or leaf curl.
recommendations: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 to 5.0) for optimal nutrient intake.
Apply organic pine needle or bark mulch to retain moisture.
Ensure consistent watering during dry periods.
prevention: Test soil acidity regularly.
Keep base clean of weeds.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to light gray powdery fungal patches on leaves and shoots, leaf curling, puckering, and stunted shoot growth.
recommendations: Prune dense canopies to maximize air movement and dry out leaves.
Apply horticultural oil or sulfur fungicides at first sign of white patches.
Remove infected new growth shoots.
prevention: Plant trees in sunny locations with good wind exposure.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Rake and bury fallen leaves in autumn.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are vibrant green, flat, and free of white patches, spots, or browning edges.
recommendations: Continue balanced watering and seasonal pruning.
Ensure orchard floor is clear of weeds.
Harvest fruit promptly to avoid fungal attractants.
prevention: Sanitize shears between pruning.
Monitor canopy density.
Keep fruit dry.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions running parallel to leaf veins, causing leaf browning and premature leaf death.
recommendations: Apply labeled foliar fungicides if lesions appear prior to tasseling.
Incorporate crop residue into the soil to accelerate decomposition.
Harvest early if stalks show lodging risks.
prevention: Use gray leaf spot resistant hybrid seed corn.
Rotate crops away from corn for at least one year.
Practice clean tillage or deep plowing.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Elongated golden-brown to cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces, causing leaf yellowing.
recommendations: Usually does not warrant fungicide application unless infection is severe and starts early.
Apply foliar fungicides only on high-value sweet corn or seed fields.
Avoid high humidity and leaf wetness.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Ensure early planting to bypass peak spore populations.
Manage field drainage.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, elliptical, grayish-green or tan lesions ('cigar-shaped') on leaves, starting on lower leaves and moving upwards.
recommendations: Apply protective fungicides during the early silk stage if lesions are visible.
Chop and till corn residue to bury wintering fungal spores.
Ensure nitrogen fertilization matches crop needs.
prevention: Choose hybrid corn seeds with strong Northern Leaf Blight resistance.
Rotate corn fields with soybeans or other non-host crops.
Avoid fields with poor air drainage.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Stalks are sturdy, and leaves are broad, dark green, and free of lesions, rust, or powdery pustules.
recommendations: Monitor soil moisture and maintain balanced fertilization.
Watch for insect pests like corn borers.
Keep fields clear of competitive weeds.
prevention: Ensure proper planting density.
Maintain high soil nutrient levels.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small brown circular spots on leaves, and shriveled, hard, black mummified berries covered in tiny black fruiting bodies.
recommendations: Remove and destroy all mummified fruit from the vine and vineyard floor.
Prune the canopy to maximize air circulation and sun exposure.
Apply copper or synthetic fungicides from bud break until bloom ends.
prevention: Keep vines off the ground using a proper trellis system.
Remove infected canes during dormant pruning.
Water early in the morning to allow leaves to dry quickly.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Interveinal yellowing or browning on leaves ('tiger-stripe' pattern), and dark spots on berries ('black measles') with skin cracking.
recommendations: Prune out diseased trunks and infected wood down to healthy tissue.
Seal pruning wounds with protective paint or paste.
Manage vine stress by avoiding over-cropping and ensuring steady water.
prevention: Use clean, certified grape cuttings for planting.
Prune grapes during dry weather to prevent wood infection.
Disinfect pruning tools between vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Dull red or brown spots on leaves that expand and dry out, leading to premature leaf drop and weakened vine vigor.
recommendations: Rake up and burn fallen leaves to prevent the fungus from overwintering.
Spray copper fungicides at the first sign of leaf spotting.
Ensure correct vine spacing for airflow.
prevention: Optimize vine pruning.
Practice clean cultivation beneath vines.
Use drip irrigation rather than sprinklers.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Vines show vigorous shoot growth, and leaves are green, broad, and free of blemishes, shriveled berries, or wood decay.
recommendations: Conduct regular vine training and suckering.
Monitor canopy density and prune shoots as needed.
Check soil moisture levels regularly.
prevention: Sanitize trellis wire and pruning tools.
Maintain vineyard floor management.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetrical leaf mottling (blotchy mottle), yellowing of shoots, small misshapen fruit that remains green at the bottom, and bitter taste.
recommendations: No cure exists. Remove and destroy infected trees to prevent spreading.
Control the vector (Asian Citrus Psyllid) using organic oils or insecticides.
Apply nutritional sprays to temporarily prolong the productive life of mildly affected trees.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock.
Monitor orchards frequently using yellow sticky traps for psyllids.
Keep orchards isolated from infected citrus groves.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark spots on leaves that turn brown and drop out ('shot-hole' appearance), and cracked, gummy spots on fruit.
recommendations: Apply copper sprays or bactericides during early spring bud swell.
Prune trees to open up the canopy and allow dry wind penetration.
Avoid applying excess nitrogen, which encourages susceptible lush growth.
prevention: Select bacterial spot resistant peach cultivars.
Maintain optimal orchard nutrition and drainage.
Prune during dry periods.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are lance-shaped, clean, rich green, and show no signs of spotting, holes, or gummy fruit lesions.
recommendations: Perform winter pruning and spring thinning.
Monitor leaves for aphids and scale insects.
Ensure proper watering during fruit development.
prevention: Sanitize tools between trees.
Keep orchard floor clear of rotting fruit.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, circular, dark spots on leaves with yellow halos, leaf drop, and raised warty spots on pepper fruits.
recommendations: Remove and destroy severely infected pepper plants.
Apply copper-based sprays every 7-14 days in wet conditions.
Avoid working in the fields when foliage is wet.
prevention: Use certified pathogen-free seeds and seedlings.
Rotate pepper crops with non-solanaceous crops for 2 years.
Practice drip irrigation to avoid splashing bacteria.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Plant foliage is bright green, smooth, and erect, showing no spots, wilt, or fruit decay.
recommendations: Water consistently to prevent blossom end rot.
Mulch to maintain stable soil temperatures.
Support heavy fruiting branches with stakes.
prevention: Rotate crops regularly.
Maintain weeding hygiene.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown, circular spots with concentric rings ('target' pattern) on older leaves, causing yellowing and leaf loss.
recommendations: Apply appropriate organic fungicides at the first sign of lower leaf spotting.
Ensure adequate soil fertility, especially nitrogen and potassium.
Remove and discard infected vines after harvest.
prevention: Plant certified seed potatoes of resistant cultivars.
Allow 3-year rotation between potato crops.
Manage watering to avoid prolonged leaf wetness.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark, water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, with a white moldy growth on leaf undersides in humid weather, leading to rapid plant rot.
recommendations: Extremely destructive. Immediately destroy all infected foliage and tubers.
Apply protective copper fungicides weekly when weather is cool and wet.
Do not compost infected plant parts; bury or burn them.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free potato tubers.
Destroy potato volunteer plants and cull piles.
Ensure wide spacing and good air circulation.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are broad, green, and free of target-like spots, water-soaked margins, or fuzzy white mold.
recommendations: Keep soil hilled around plant bases to protect developing tubers.
Irrigate early in the morning so foliage dries by midday.
Monitor leaves for potato beetles.
prevention: Use crop rotation schedules.
Ensure optimal soil drainage.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Leaves are serrated, green, and flat, showing no signs of yellowing, rust pustules, or leaf spots.
recommendations: Prune canes annually to maintain a manageable row width and airflow.
Provide trellis support for climbing canes.
Mulch to maintain organic matter and conserve moisture.
prevention: Sanitize pruning tools between rows.
Remove old fruited canes in winter.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Tri-foliate leaves are dark green and clean, free of rust, mildew, spots, or mosaic discoloration.
recommendations: Keep fields clear of competitive weeds.
Monitor canopy closure and spacing.
Perform periodic checks for soybean rust.
prevention: Practice balanced crop rotation.
Use certified seed stock.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum-like white powdery spots on leaves and stems, leading to yellowing, drying, and premature leaf death.
recommendations: Prune overlapping leaves to allow sun exposure and dry the canopy.
Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or sulfur-based fungicides.
Avoid excess nitrogen, which triggers susceptible soft growth.
prevention: Select powdery mildew resistant squash varieties.
Plant squash in full sun locations.
Water plants at the base via drip tubes.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Irregular dark-purple spots on leaves that expand and turn brown, making the leaf margins look dry, scorched, and paper-like.
recommendations: Remove and burn infected leaves or renovate the bed after harvest.
Apply copper fungicides in early spring to suppress spores.
Ensure proper weed control to improve wind drying.
prevention: Plant disease-free runner plants.
Avoid planting in heavy, poorly drained clay soils.
Renovate strawberry beds every 2-3 years.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Foliage is green, low-growing, and free of dark purple spots or scorched margins. Berries form cleanly.
recommendations: Apply clean straw mulch to keep berries off the soil.
Irrigate regularly during fruit production.
Prune excess runners to focus energy on fruit.
prevention: Replace old plants every few years.
Sanitize garden beds.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves and stems, with yellow halos, leading to leaf drop and small raised black spots on tomatoes.
recommendations: Prune lower leaves to reduce soil-to-leaf bacterial splash.
Apply copper-based bactericides at the first sign of symptoms.
Remove and destroy heavily infested tomato vines immediately.
prevention: Always use certified disease-free seeds and transplants.
Avoid handling tomato plants when they are wet.
Practice crop rotation out of tomatoes for 2 years.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric rings ('target' appearance) on older leaves starting at the bottom of the plant, causing leaf yellowing, browning, and defoliation.
recommendations: Trim away lower branches to keep foliage at least 12 inches above the soil.
Avoid overhead watering; use drip irrigation.
Apply protective fungicides (copper or chlorothalonil) if weather is wet.
prevention: Apply mulch around the base of the plant to prevent soil splash.
Rotate crops away from potatoes and tomatoes.
Space plants at least 24 inches apart.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, dark brown water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, accompanied by white fuzzy growth on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
recommendations: Very contagious. Immediately pull up and discard the entire infected plant.
Keep tomatoes pruned for rapid drying.
Apply copper fungicides preemptively during cool, wet periods.
prevention: Grow tomatoes in greenhouse tunnels or under cover in rain-prone areas.
Avoid planting near potatoes.
Clean cages and stakes at season end.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellow spots on upper leaf surfaces, with olive-green velvety mold growth on corresponding leaf undersides in high humidity.
recommendations: Increase ventilation in greenhouses or pruning density outdoors.
Ensure night temperatures do not cause condensation on leaves.
Apply preventative copper fungicides if humidity remains high.
prevention: Maintain humidity levels below 85% in greenhouses.
Plant resistant tomato varieties.
Avoid high canopy density.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small, circular spots with dark brown margins and gray centers containing tiny black specks on lower leaves.
recommendations: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves immediately.
Apply mulch to create a barrier between soil-borne spores and foliage.
Spray copper or organic fungicides if spots begin to spread upward.
prevention: Clean cages and stakes thoroughly before planting.
Rotate fields out of tomatoes for 2 years.
Avoid handling plants when leaves are wet.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow speckling or stippling on leaves, followed by leaf bronzing, drying, and fine webbing on leaf undersides and stems.
recommendations: Spray leaves with strong water jets to knock down mites and webs.
Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, or sulfur sprays.
Introduce natural predators like predatory mites.
prevention: Avoid dusty conditions which favor mite reproduction.
Keep plants adequately watered to minimize drought stress.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Dark brown, circular lesions on leaves, stems, and fruit, showing light brown centers with target-like rings, causing leaf dropping.
recommendations: Prune lower leaves to improve canopy aeration.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.
Apply protective fungicides when warm, humid weather persists.
prevention: Maintain a 3-year crop rotation.
Bury or remove crop debris post-harvest.
Ensure proper vine staking.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe stunting, leaves curling upward and inward, leaf margins turning yellow, and complete failure to set fruit.
recommendations: Virus is transmitted by whiteflies. Control whiteflies using yellow sticky cards and insecticidal soaps.
Immediately pull out and bag infected plants to prevent vector transmission.
Weed the garden area to eliminate alternative hosts.
prevention: Use whitefly-resistant tomato hybrid varieties.
Protect young seedlings with row covers.
Keep greenhouses sealed against insects.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green patterns ('mosaic') on leaves, leaf distortion (shoestring-like shape), and uneven fruit ripening.
recommendations: Highly infectious via contact. Immediately pull up and burn/bury infected plants.
Wash hands and tools with soap and water after handling tomatoes.
Avoid touching healthy plants after contact with infected ones.
prevention: Plant mosaic-resistant tomato seeds.
Disinfect garden stakes and cages with bleach solution.
Avoid smoking near tomato crops, as tobacco can carry the virus.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Vines are strong, and leaves are broad, dark green, and flat, showing no spots, curling, wilting, or fuzzy fungal growths.
recommendations: Prune suckers regularly to maintain single/double main vine stems.
Mulch around the base and water at the root level.
Monitor weekly for hornworms or leaf spot signs.
prevention: Maintain sanitization protocols.
Ensure good crop spacing.
